editorial:
Imagine you are just trying to live a quiet life as a mechanic, but then one day, a ghost from your past walks right into your shop. You get to see the world through the eyes of a man who spent years in a scary Iranian prison, only to come face-to-face with the guy who made his life a living hell back then. The vibe is very tense and makes you feel the pressure building up as the main character tries to decide if he should move on or get some payback. It is a slow burn that keeps you guessing about what will happen next.

What really makes this work is the acting, as both leads feel like real people you would meet on the street. The pacing is steady, though some might find the middle a bit slow, but the payoff is totally worth it. If you love stories about revenge and secrets, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the mechanic traps his former captor in the garage. He wants a confession for the crimes committed in prison. However, the twist is that the captor is now a broken man who does not even remember the torture he caused. Instead of killing him, the mechanic realizes that seeing the man so pathetic is a better punishment than death. He lets him go, finally finding peace and letting go of his anger.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about revenge.
